title: High-fanout multipart requests causing transient 502s — isolate, fastpatch, and resilience plan
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Summary:
A subset of customers observed elevated 5xx (502/504) rates when issuing high-fanout multipart inference requests (batch-style uploads that fan out to multiple model shards/proxies). The errors started 2025-01-11 03:00 UTC and correlate with an increase in concurrent multipart streaming from 3 tenants during a migration window.

Observed behavior:
- Request path: frontdoor -> edge-proxy -> multipart combiner -> inference gateway -> runtime pool
- Errors are predominantly 502 (bad gateway) and 504 (gateway timeout) returned by our edge-proxy / combiner layer; downstream runtime logs show many short-lived connection resets and RetryableError surfaces.
- Retried clients amplified traffic; some proxies hit connection table limits leading to cascading failovers.
- KV cache compaction events happened concurrently for two nodes; hypothesis: compaction combined with heavy fanout increased tail latencies and triggered early upstream timeouts.

Immediate mitigating actions taken (fastpatch timeline):
- 2025-01-11 04:00 UTC: Raised tenant priority and applied per-tenant soft admission window to stop retries from spiraling (temporary throttle).
- 2025-01-11 04:30 UTC: Deployed edge-proxy knob to coalesce multipart subrequests for tenants with active session affinity (PR: github.com/redwood/edge/PR-1208).
- 2025-01-11 05:15 UTC: Rolled out a defensive inflight semaphore on the combiner service to cap concurrent fanout per request (hotpatch).
- Result: error rate dropped ~78% for affected tenants within 45 minutes, but we still see intermittent 502s under peak load.

Root-cause hypothesis (current):
1) High concurrent multipart fanout created a short-lived spike in connection churn and per-proxy connection-table exhaustion.
2) Simultaneous KV-cache compaction increased runtime response tail latency; upstream timeouts were triggered while clients retried, amplifying load.
3) Edge-proxy did not coalesce multipart subrequests efficiently for these tenants, increasing fanout multiplicatively.

Planned durable fixes and acceptance criteria:
- Short-term (this sprint):
  * Finalize and roll out edge-proxy multipart coalescer (config flag: coalesce_multipart=true) with per-tenant stickiness. Acceptance: <1% 502s at 95th percentile under replayed surge. Owner: @Liam Torres.
  * Instrument and surface a new "fanout_concurrency" metric in Grafana for combiner and gateway. Acceptance: dashboards show per-tenant concurrency correlated with errors. Owner: @Priya Anand.
- Medium-term (next 2 sprints):
  * Implement adaptive inflight semaphore automatically driven by real-time connection table utilization (policy engine change). Acceptance: prevents connection-table exhaustion during bursty fanout workloads. Owner: @Marco Ruiz.
  * Add pre-fanout prefix caching and small-response streaming to reduce downstream calls for repeated prefixes. Acceptance: measurable reduction in byte-level fanout per request. Owner: @Sofia Kim.
- Long-term:
  * KV-cache compaction backoff: ensure compaction does not coincide with high ingress windows (operator schedule + automatic pause on surge).
  * Add a "fanout-safe" routing path that prefers low-concurrency nodes for multipart jobs.

Rollback matrix and rollout plan:
- Canary: enable coalescer for 2 internal tenants and run 6-hour soak; monitor error rate, p95 latency, connection-table occupancy.
- Rollforward: if errors drop and no regressions in p99 latency, expand to 20% of customers, then 50%, then full.
- Rollback triggers: increase in p99 latency > 15% or connection_table_util > 85% for two consecutive 5m windows.

Observability & tracing additions:
- Add a combiner-span attribute "fanout_count" and propagate to traces.
- Tag inflight semaphore hits and surface as an index in SLO dashboards.
- Alert: new alert for "edge-proxy_coalesce_failures" to catch cases where coalescer cannot reduce downstream calls.

Follow-ups / Postmortem items:
- Postmortem doc in Confluence: link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-246814+fanout+postmortem
- Customer comms template drafted and staged for PM review (Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/fanout-comm).
- Run a chaos test simulating concurrent KV compaction + fanout bursts in staging (owner: @Sofia Kim).

Notes on customer escalations:
- Two customers (Customer A and Customer B) opened P0 tickets; both were given temporary admission windows and a priority bridge. Customer success is scheduled for a 2025-01-19 update call.
- Legal requested a record of all commits and rollouts touching the edge-proxy for the incident window (log links included in comments).
